title: You felt something when you first heard it.
paragraphs: You felt something when you first heard it.

A stirring.
A fire.
A sense that God wasn’t distant… He was moving.
And then somewhere along the way, it got confusing.

People shouting “gift of the Spirit” while living in quiet sin.
Manifestations with no Scripture.
Churches either chasing power… or denying it entirely.
So now you’re left asking—maybe not out loud, but deep inside—

Are spiritual gifts still real…
or have we turned them into something God never intended?
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The question isn’t whether spiritual gifts are active.
The real question is whether we are aligned with the Spirit who gives them.
Because the Bible doesn’t stutter here.
“Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.” — 1 Corinthians 12:1

Not confused.
Not manipulated.
Not entertained.
Informed.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
And yet look around.
You’ve seen it.

People claiming prophecy but contradicting Scripture.
Tongues without interpretation.
Healing services that feel more like performance than prayer.
Leaders building platforms instead of pointing to Christ.
God saw it.
And if you’re honest…
You knew something felt off.
Because the same Spirit who gives gifts is the Spirit of truth.
“God is not a God of confusion but of peace.” — 1 Corinthians 14:33
Read that again.

So if it’s chaotic, self-centered, or disconnected from the Gospel—
it’s not the Spirit of God.
But don’t swing to the other extreme.
Because some have reacted to misuse by rejecting the gifts entirely.

They shut it all down.
Label everything supernatural as fake.
Reduce Christianity to intellect and routine.
But Scripture never says the gifts would cease before Christ returns.
In fact—
“To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.” — 1 Corinthians 12:7
Each.
That includes you.

Not for hype.
Not for status.
Not for control.
For the common good.

For building the Body.
For revealing Christ.
For advancing the Gospel.
So what happened?
Here’s the tension most people avoid…

Spiritual gifts are still active—
but many are being misused by people who aren’t surrendered.
That’s the fracture.
Because gifts can function through someone who lacks intimacy with God.

Judas performed miracles.
But he never belonged to Christ.
Let that settle.

You can move in something supernatural…
and still be spiritually lost.
That’s why Paul says—
“If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels but have not love, I am a noisy gong…” — 1 Corinthians 13:1
Noise.
Empty.
Impressive on the outside… hollow within.
So now the line is drawn.

Not between “gifts vs no gifts”
but between
Spirit-filled vs self-driven.
Because when the Holy Spirit truly moves, it always does three things:

It exalts Jesus.
It aligns with Scripture.
It produces holiness.
Anything else… is imitation.
And this is where it gets personal.
Because maybe you’re not shouting in a service or claiming visions—
but you’ve still reduced the Spirit to something manageable.
Safe.
Predictable.

You read the Word without expecting power.
You pray without expecting response.
You live like the supernatural ended in Acts.
But Jesus said—
“You will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you…” — Acts 1:8
Power.
Not for spectacle.
For witness.
For transformation.
For a life that cannot be explained apart from God.
So now you’re standing in the middle of it.

One side abusing the gifts.
The other side denying them.
And God is calling you somewhere deeper.
Not to chase experiences.
Not to suppress truth.
But to return to Him.
Because the gifts were never the goal.
Jesus is.
Always has been.
And here’s the Gospel that brings clarity to all of it—
You don’t receive the Spirit because you’re spiritual.
You receive the Spirit because Christ died for your sin.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

That includes the loud preacher.
The quiet skeptic.
The wounded believer.
All.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not after you got it right.
Not after you understood spiritual gifts.
While you were still broken.

And when you repent—truly turn—
and place your faith in Jesus Christ…
You are forgiven.
Made new.
Filled with the Holy Spirit.
Not a counterfeit version.
Not emotional hype.
The real presence of God.
And yes—
He still gives gifts.
But now they flow from surrender, not performance.
From relationship, not reputation.
From truth, not confusion.
So here’s where it lands.
You can keep watching from a distance, trying to figure it out.

Or you can come to Christ, receive His Spirit, and walk in truth—
not chasing gifts, but stewarding what He gives.
Because one day, none of the noise will matter.
Only this—

Did you know Him?
Or did you just move around Him?
If something in you is unsettled right now… that’s not random.
That’s conviction.
Say it plainly if it’s real—
“Jesus, I want what is true—not what is fake.”
Let that be your starting point.

If this exposed something in you, don’t keep it silent.
Write it. Own it. Bring it into the light.
There are people in your life confused about this too—send this to them.
Follow this path if you’re done with surface-level faith and want depth that actually transforms.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—to be corrected, sharpened, and built up in truth, not hype—
Not more noise.

Truth that cuts.
Truth that heals.
Truth that leads you to Christ.
